# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Riley Foster**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Banner Health — Member Appeals
*Send to the appeal address printed on the denial letter, or call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.*

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated **August 22, 2026** — Reference number **POC-D5606CAED3-36942**
**Member:** Riley Foster | **Member ID:** W204716433
**Plan:** Banner Health (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT **29827**
**Governing policy:** *eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery — Arthroscopic and Open Procedures*, https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-315%20Shoulder%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf
**This appeal must be received by:** **February 18, 2027**

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 22, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Banner Health to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure, because the records already in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria — including its imaging criteria.

Below, I have quoted the plan's criteria word for word and matched each one to what my records say.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging — the reason given for the denial**

The policy states:

> "MRI or CT shows EITHER of the following findings:"

> "Grade 2 or 3 partial-thickness rotator cuff tear (Ellman classification)"

> "Full-thickness rotator cuff tear (Cofield classification)"

My MRI of the shoulder dated **July 6, 2026** shows a **full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm**, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. A full-thickness rotator cuff tear is one of the two imaging findings the policy accepts, and only one is required. This is the specific point on which the request was denied, and the imaging report in my file states the finding directly.

**2. Physical exam findings**

The policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH the following findings (as compared to the non- involved side):"

> "Functionally-limited range of motion"

> "Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature"

My exam records document **range of motion limited by pain**, and I **cannot lift my arm above shoulder height**. For the strength element and the comparison to my other shoulder, please see [measured strength testing of the affected and non-involved shoulder, as documented in Dr. Okafor's exam note dated [date]], which I ask that the reviewer obtain from my surgeon's office if it is not already in the file.

**3. Positive orthopedic tests or signs**

The policy states:

> "ANY of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs:"

and the list of tests in the excerpt I have includes:

> "Drop a rm test  Painful arc test  Jobe or empty can test  External rotation lag sign (dropping sign)  Internal rotation lag sign  Lift-off test  Bear hug test  Belly-press test (Napoleon)  Belly-off t"

My records state **positive provocative testing on the affected side**. The specific test names are recorded as [names of the positive orthopedic tests from Dr. Okafor's exam note dated [date]]. Only one positive test or sign is required under this heading.

**4. Function-limiting pain**

The policy states:

> "Function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment)"

I have had **18 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest**. I **cannot lift my arm above shoulder height** and I **cannot sleep on the affected side**. These are everyday activities, and the loss of function is why I am seeking surgery.

**5. Non-surgical management**

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration"

My documented provider-directed non-surgical care includes:

- **NSAIDs for 4 months**, with inadequate relief;
- a **corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026**, which gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief;
- **supervised physical therapy** focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, **24 visits over 10 weeks from April 17, 2026 through June 26, 2026**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

I also want to address the fatty atrophy on my MRI directly, because the policy speaks to it. The policy states:

> "Note: The pr esence of fatty infiltration and/or muscle atrophy on MRI or CT is considered evidence of pre-existing chronic rotator cuff tear."

and:

> "Therefore, when fatty infiltration and/or muscle atrophy is also present on MRI or CT, three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is required, regardless of whether a discrete traumatic event occurred."

I am not relying on the traumatic-injury exception, which the policy words as follows:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required for an individual who suffers a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear without evidence of a pre-existing chronic rotator cuff tear."

Instead, I am pointing to the non-surgical management I actually completed: four months of NSAIDs, an injection, and a full supervised physical therapy course of 24 visits, all of which failed to relieve my symptoms. If Banner Health reads the duration requirement differently as applied to my records, I ask that the plan state specifically which dates and which treatments it counted and which it did not.

**6. Other conditions excluded**

The policy states:

> "Other potential pathological cond itions have been excluded including, but not limited to, the following: fracture, thoracic outlet syndrome, brachial plexus disorders, referred neck pain, and advanced glenohumeral osteoarthritis"

Please see [Dr. Okafor's documentation addressing the exclusion of these other conditions], which I ask the reviewer to obtain from my surgeon's office if it is not already in my file.

## A note about the criteria I was able to review

Several of the excerpts I have from the policy end in a colon and introduce lists that were not reproduced in the material available to me, and one list of orthopedic tests is cut off mid-word. The policy therefore contains further conditions and list items that I have not seen and am not able to quote. I have quoted only the plan's own language, exactly as it appears, and I have not paraphrased or reconstructed any of it. I ask Banner Health to identify, in writing, the precise criterion or criteria from *eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery — Arthroscopic and Open Procedures* that my request was found not to meet, so that I can respond to the specific point.

## What I am requesting

I respectfully ask Banner Health to:

1. Overturn the denial dated August 22, 2026 (reference POC-D5606CAED3-36942) and authorize rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with experience in orthopedic shoulder surgery;
3. Obtain and consider the complete records from Dr. Okafor's office and my physical therapy discharge note, if any part of the file is missing; and
4. Provide a written explanation identifying the specific policy criterion relied upon if the denial is upheld, along with information about any further appeal rights, including external review.

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed. My MRI shows the full-thickness tear the policy names, I have significant loss of function, and I completed and failed months of non-surgical treatment. I am asking the plan to compare its own criteria to my records and reconsider.

I have enclosed: [list of enclosures — e.g., MRI report dated 2026-07-06, physical therapy discharge note, office notes from Dr. Okafor, copy of the denial notice].

Thank you for your time and for a careful second look.

Sincerely,

**Riley Foster**
Member ID: W204716433
[Signature]
[Date]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
